sections.html:
Fillmore County sits in southeastern Nebraska with Geneva as the county seat, the only city. The villages are Exeter, Fairmont, Grafton, Milligan, Ohiowa, Shickley and Strang. The 2020 census counted 5,551 residents and the 2025 estimate is 5,458, so the county is small and slowly shrinking. Farming, mostly corn and soybeans, is the main economy.

Housing units numbered 2,718 in 2020, and 12.2% of them stood vacant. That much slack means a house that needs work can sit for a while on the open market. Sellers with a vacant inherited home or a rental they no longer want to manage often weigh that wait against another year of carrying costs and taxes.

Many houses and farmsteads date to the 1870s, when the railroad opened the area. On an older property, buyers ask first about the roof, the wiring and the foundation. Lots in low spots on the flat loess plain can hold water after heavy rain or snowmelt, so look at drainage before you list.

Real estate and personal property taxes in Fillmore County turn delinquent on May 1 and September 1, and interest starts on those dates at 14 percent (Nebraska statutes 77-203 and 77-204). Notices go out around December 1.

Deadline or feeFillmore County rule
First half delinquentMay 1
Second half delinquentSeptember 1
Weekend or holidayIf April 30 or August 31 falls on one, the next business day is the last day to pay without interest
Mailed paymentsJudged by postmark
Card payments2.35 percent convenience fee

The treasurer no longer has to mail paid receipts, so enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope if you want one. Amounts and payment status are on the Nebraska Taxes Online website, or you can call the treasurer. If a notice never arrives, call the office, because a missing notice doesn't move the due date. To change a mailing address, call or use the county's change of address form.

When a house changes hands early in the year, the first half of the prior year's bill is often still open until May 1. Ask the closing agent to show exactly which half is being paid and by whom.

You challenge the valuation, not the tax bill. File Nebraska Form 422 with the county clerk, who staffs the County Board of Equalization, by June 30 for real property. The form comes from the Nebraska Department of Revenue.

The protest has to state the value you're asking for and why. A board decision can be appealed to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission within 30 days after the board adjourns, and for the June 1 to July 25 session the adjournment date is deemed to be July 25.

Good evidence is a recent sale of a similar house nearby, a repair estimate that explains a lower condition, or proof that your property is valued out of line with comparable ones. For a failing roof, a cracked foundation or other major defects, photos and contractor bids carry more weight than opinion.

Rural acreage may be taxed as agricultural land, which follows different valuation rules from a town lot.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes can land in the county treasurer's annual tax sale, held the first Monday in March at 9:00 a.m. at the courthouse. Delinquent parcels are advertised in the local paper for three consecutive weeks in February and on Nebraska Taxes Online.

The buyer purchases a tax lien, not the house. The redemption period is three years, the certificate earns 14 percent, and the buyer must pay later years' delinquent taxes to keep the certificate alive. If the owner hasn't redeemed by the end of three years, the certificate holder has six months to start foreclosure.

That makes February a real deadline. Selling before the advertising run keeps the parcel off the public list, and advertising charges are added to what a certificate buyer pays. The treasurer can't give legal advice, so ask a Nebraska attorney about certificates and redemption.

Nebraska's documentary stamp tax is $3.32 for each $1,000 of value, or fraction of $1,000, on deeds recorded as of July 18, 2026. It falls on the grantor, who is the seller. Every deed also needs a completed Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, which the register of deeds won't accept if it's incomplete.

Exemptions exist for some transfers, such as certain deeds to trustees. A title company or closing attorney normally prepares both items. Ask for the figure on your estimated settlement statement so nothing surprises you at the table.

sections.h2: Roads, towns and who buys here
sections.html:
US 81 enters from Thayer County and runs north into York County. US 6 crosses the northern part of the county, Nebraska Highway 41 runs through the middle and Highway 74 follows the south. BNSF Railway tracks pass Exeter, Fairmont and Grafton in the north.

  • Houses along US 6 and the rail line in Exeter, Fairmont and Grafton draw a different pool of buyers than farmsteads off county gravel.
  • Geneva holds the courthouse, the county offices and the schools, so it tends to anchor local interest.
  • A listing agent in a county this small may bring few showings in a month, which is why some owners ask for a cash offer instead.

sections.h2: Selling a Fillmore County house with a deadline
sections.html:
Whether the house is inherited, behind on taxes or simply tired, a few steps keep the sale moving:

  • Ask the treasurer or closing agent for the exact payoff and which half-year is open.
  • Decide whether to protest, which must be filed by June 30, or to sell and let the buyer deal with the next valuation.
  • If the parcel is heading toward the February tax sale ad, aim to close before it runs.
  • Have your title company prepare the deed and Form 521.

Cash Home Buyers can review a Fillmore County house and explain how an as-is offer would work. The title company settles taxes with the treasurer from your proceeds, and a cash sale skips showings, lender appraisals and repair negotiations.

faqs.q: When are Fillmore County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: May 1 and September 1, with interest at 14 percent starting those dates. If April 30 or August 31 falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day is the last day to pay without interest.

faqs.q: Where do I file a property valuation protest in Fillmore County?
faqs.a: File Nebraska Form 422 with the county clerk, who handles the County Board of Equalization. Real property protests are due by June 30 and must state the value you want and the reason.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fillmore County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent taxes are normally paid from the proceeds at closing, and the closing agent can request a payoff figure from the treasurer. Selling before the February advertising keeps the parcel off the public list.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Fillmore County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor. The rate is $3.32 for each $1,000 of value on deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, subject to any exemption that applies.

faqs.q: How can I check what I owe the Fillmore County treasurer?
faqs.a: Look up amounts and payment status on Nebraska Taxes Online, or call the treasurer's office through the county website.
